In the plural number with the article
ή θεός [the goddess] goddess.

The oblique cases of the noun θεός [god] and the nominative θεοί [gods] sometimes become monosyllabic through synizesis, in Sophocles, about which I have spoken in the Lexicon Sophocleum p. 221, and in Euripides more frequently than in Aeschylus.
